title: Michelle Riconscente, PhD (CEO & Co-Founder, Valutare) — five takeaways from Eric's Responsive Conference closing keynote: 'Trust is an asset. Ries called it the Culture Bank'
summary: Michelle Riconscente, PhD — CEO & Co-Founder of Valutare, author of 'The AI Amplification Effect' — publishes a crisp five-point recap of Eric's Responsive Conference closing keynote (hosted by Jamie Lynn White). Introduces one of the sharpest new frames from the tour: the 'Culture Bank' — every time a company does the right thing at a real cost to itself, it makes a deposit; every short-term spreadsheet-driven compromise makes a withdrawal.
blockquote: Yesterday at Responsive Conference, Jamie Lynn White hosted a fantastic closing keynote by Eric Ries. My favorite part? His points about the need to rethink performance management, of course! Trust is an asset. Ries called it the "Culture Bank": every time a company does the right thing at a real cost to itself, it makes a deposit. Every short-term, spreadsheet-driven compromise makes a withdrawal. Mission needs infrastructure, not posters. We build serious systems to ensure financial compliance. If mission is truly core, it should have real accountability, rituals, and decision-making weight too.
blockquote_source: Michelle Riconscente, PhD on LinkedIn, summarizing Eric Ries at Responsive Conference
